correctness.rationale: The centralization lemma is valid for every rectangle in a centrally symmetric convex body: each centered vertex \(\pm u\pm v\) is the midpoint of an original vertex and the centrally reflected opposite original vertex, so convexity preserves containment and area. For a centered rectangle the half-diagonals have common length \(r\) and area \(2r^2\sin\delta\). In a regular n-gon the radial reach at angular offset \(s\) from a vertex ray is \(\cos\alpha/\cos(\alpha-s)\), \(\alpha=\pi/n\). When \(4\mid n\), \(r\le R\) and \(\sin\delta\le1\) are simultaneously sharp at orthogonal vertex rays. When \(n\equiv2\pmod4\), the largest acute separation of vertex lines is \(\delta_0=\pi/2-\alpha\). For \(\delta=\delta_0+t\), nearest-vertex offsets satisfy \(s_1+s_2\ge t\), so the common radius is at most \(R\cos\alpha/\cos(\alpha-t/2)\); the identity \(\cos^2(\alpha-t/2)-\cos\alpha\cos(\alpha-t)=(1-\cos t)/2\) proves strict loss for every \(t>0\). This reconstructs both formula branches and the centered equality cases.
